hero.headline: Trump confronts Netanyahu over Lebanon escalation in expletive-laden call
hero.body:
President Trump engaged in a heated phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over Israel's military escalation in Lebanon, according to two U.S. officials and a third source briefed on the exchange. During the Monday conversation, Trump used profanity to criticize Netanyahu, calling him "crazy" and accusing him of ingratitude. He also intervened to block Israel's planned strike on Beirut.

The confrontation underscores growing tensions between the Trump administration and Netanyahu's government as the region faces mounting instability. The call came after Iran warned it would withdraw from ongoing negotiations with the United States in response to Israeli military operations in Lebanon. That same day, Netanyahu announced he had ordered the military to escalate its offensive against Hezbollah, stating his goal was to "crush" the organization.

According to the sources, Trump told Netanyahu that attacking Beirut would further damage Israel's international standing. One U.S. official noted that Trump referenced his past support for Netanyahu, suggesting the prime minister should be grateful for American backing. The decision to halt the planned strike represented an unusual constraint on Israeli military operations that reflected the seriousness of the dispute.

The escalating conflict in Lebanon has intensified despite a ceasefire that began in April. Both Israel and Hezbollah have continued exchanging fire on a near-daily basis. In recent days, Israel has carried out extensive airstrikes across southern Lebanon, the Bekaa Valley, and areas near Tyre. Lebanese authorities report that Israeli strikes since March have killed more than 3,100 people. Hezbollah has responded with drone attacks on Israeli military positions and border areas, with multiple strikes occurring on Monday.

Netanyahu's call for intensified operations has found support among far-right members of his government. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for ending the threat posed by Hezbollah's drone attacks, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir demanded a return to intensive warfare and expansion of Israeli-controlled territory.

The situation reflects broader complications in Middle East diplomacy. Iran's decision to threaten withdrawal from U.S. negotiations signals how Israeli military actions directly influence diplomatic engagement with Tehran. However, Trump expressed indifference about the status of those talks during a separate Monday interview with CNBC, stating he did not care whether negotiations with Iran continued, calling them "very boring."

The disconnect between Trump's intervention to block the Beirut strike and his dismissive comments about Iran talks creates uncertainty about the administration's strategic priorities. The U.S.-Israel relationship and prospects for broader regional diplomacy remain in flux as the conflict continues to develop and both sides pursue escalation.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Climb After U.S.-Iran Military Strikes
cards.teaser: Oil prices rose as the United States and Iran exchanged military fire while continuing diplomatic negotiations.
cards.body:
Oil prices rose 6 percent following military strikes between the United States and Iran over the weekend, including attacks on Iranian sites near Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Investors are assessing the potential impact on global energy supplies amid the escalating tensions.

Analysts cautioned that oil prices could climb substantially higher if the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global oil transport, remains disrupted. Meanwhile, both countries have halted direct negotiations, with Iran suspending talks over U.S. support for Israeli operations in Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: Trump administration requires most Medicaid beneficiaries to work
cards.teaser: A new rule mandates that most Medicaid recipients between 19 and 64 prove employment, community service, or work program participation to receive benefits.
cards.body:
The Trump administration issued a final rule requiring most Medicaid beneficiaries between the ages of 19 and 64 to demonstrate they work, complete community service, or participate in a work program to qualify for benefits. The rule establishes standards that states must follow when implementing the Medicaid work requirements mandated by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

The rule outlines broad policies each state is required to have in place when enforcing the new work requirements. The change represents a significant shift in how the federal health insurance program for low-income Americans operates, adding employment conditions to eligibility criteria that previously focused primarily on income levels.

cards.headline: European Union approves strictest-ever migration law with return hubs
cards.teaser: EU negotiators agree to fast-track deportation system as hardening views shift policy.
cards.body:
The European Union has reached a deal on new migration laws that will allow for faster deportation of illegal migrants, including the establishment of return hubs. The agreement represents the strictest migration legislation the bloc has ever approved, reflecting a shift in European policy.

The deal paves the way for migrant deportation centers to be established outside the EU's borders. Negotiators described the new law as enabling fast-tracked returns, marking a significant change in how the bloc handles migration and border control.

cards.headline: Pentagon bars reporters from press office, designates area classified
cards.teaser: The Defense Department has closed its press office to journalists and designated the space as classified, ending years of direct reporter access.
cards.body:
The Pentagon barred reporters from entering the building's press office and designated the facility as a classified space, ending access journalists have had for years. The Defense Department's public affairs office previously allowed reporters to approach military public affairs officials without escorts and ask questions directly.

The change curtails a longstanding arrangement that gave journalists working space within the Pentagon and direct access to public affairs staff. Reporters will no longer be able to enter the area where they could interact with military communications officials on an informal basis.

cards.headline: Justice Department to pause work on $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund after court ruling
cards.teaser: The Justice Department said it would abide by a court order pausing its fund for victims of government weaponization, though it strongly disagrees with the ruling.
cards.body:
The Justice Department announced it will comply with a court order halting a $1.776 billion fund created to compensate victims of government "weaponization." Although the department expressed strong disagreement with the court's decision, it said it would follow the ruling.

The fund has faced significant opposition in Congress and the courts throughout its existence. The Trump administration is signaling a retreat from the controversial initiative, which had been a prominent part of its agenda.

cards.headline: Trump ends rebate program for switching to electric appliances
cards.teaser: The Energy Department reinterpreted an Inflation Reduction Act program, eliminating cash rebates for Americans who purchase high-efficiency electric appliances.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has eliminated a rebate program that provided cash incentives for homeowners to purchase high-efficiency electric appliances. The Energy Department issued new guidance reinterpreting the initiative, which was created through the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act to encourage Americans to transition from gas to electric appliances.

The rebate mechanism, established by Congress two years prior, is no longer available under the Trump administration's revised interpretation of the program.

hero.headline: White House pushes Iran for deal as Tehran demands concessions
hero.teaser: Trump administration faces pressure from polls and Gulf allies to secure agreement with Iran.
hero.body:
Trump is reviewing a proposed memorandum of understanding drafted by American and Iranian diplomats with help from Pakistan and Qatar. The agreement would extend the current ceasefire for 60 days while negotiations continue on a permanent peace accord.

The requested changes focus on the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium. Iran has maintained its positions despite the administration's diplomatic efforts to reach terms.

cards.headline: European Union approves strictest-ever migration law with return hubs
cards.teaser: EU negotiators agree to fast-track deportation system as hardening views shift policy.
cards.body:
The European Union has reached a deal on new migration laws that will allow for faster deportation of illegal migrants, including the establishment of return hubs. The agreement represents the strictest migration legislation the bloc has ever approved, reflecting a shift in European policy.

The deal paves the way for migrant deportation centers to be established outside the EU's borders. Negotiators described the new law as enabling fast-tracked returns, marking a significant change in how the bloc handles migration and border control.

cards.headline: Two possible Ebola cases in Brazil ruled out after negative tests
cards.teaser: Patients who recently returned from DR Congo and Uganda test negative for the virus.
cards.body:
Two patients in Brazil who were suspected of having Ebola have tested negative for the virus. Both individuals had recently returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, where an Ebola outbreak is ongoing.

The negative results eliminate the possibility of Ebola spreading to Brazil. If confirmed, these would have been the first cases outside Africa since the outbreak began in the DR Congo.

cards.headline: Syrian officers face war crimes trial in Austria for alleged torture
cards.teaser: First prosecution of Assad regime officials in Austria gives Syrian witnesses chance to testify.
cards.body:
Two Syrian officers who had been living in Austria are facing war crimes charges in the country's first trial against Assad regime officials. The men are accused of torture by Syrian witnesses who will have the opportunity to confront them in court.

The trial represents a rare case where officials from the Assad regime face prosecution in Europe. The officers had been hiding in plain sight in Austria before being charged with war crimes related to their actions during the Syrian conflict.

cards.headline: Alberta to hold vote on whether to pursue separation from Canada
cards.teaser: Residents will decide in October whether province should hold referendum on leaving Canada.
cards.body:
Albertans will vote in October on whether they want to remain in Canada or hold a referendum on separating from the country. The vote gives the province's separatist movement its most significant opportunity to advance its goals.

The outcome could either settle the question of Alberta's place in Canada or deepen existing divisions. The movement has gained momentum in recent years, and the upcoming vote will test the extent of support for separating from the federal government.

cards.headline: Florida sues OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT aided mass shooters
cards.teaser: Attorney General claims company and CEO Sam Altman built web of deceit.
cards.body:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company failed to warn users that ChatGPT could be dangerous. Instead, OpenAI allegedly marketed the chatbot as safe and reliable, according to the complaint.

The lawsuit centers on a shooting at Florida State University and ChatGPT's alleged role in the incident. Uthmeier accuses OpenAI of building what he described as a web of deceit regarding the chatbot's safety capabilities.

cards.headline: AI company Anthropic plans to list shares on US stock market
cards.teaser: Maker of Claude chatbot to offer public shares sometime this year.
cards.body:
Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, has confidentially filed for an initial public offering on the US stock market. The filing comes as the artificial intelligence industry sees heightened investor interest, with multiple AI-related firms preparing to go public this year.

The company recently raised $65 billion in funding, valuing it at $965 billion. This represents significant growth from its $380 billion valuation in February. Claude has gained traction among software engineers and business clients, establishing Anthropic as a major competitor in the generative AI space.

hero.headline: Iran suspends talks with US over Israeli operations in Lebanon and Gaza
hero.teaser: Iran has halted negotiations with the United States over Israeli military actions in southern Lebanon and Gaza.
hero.body:
Iran has suspended diplomatic talks with the United States, citing Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon and Gaza. The decision marks a significant interruption to ongoing negotiations aimed at de-escalating the regional conflict.

President Trump stated that Israel and Hezbollah would cease fighting once Iran halted its talks with the U.S. The White House had been pursuing a comprehensive agreement to end hostilities across the region, but the breakdown in Iran-U.S. negotiations has complicated those broader diplomatic efforts.

cards.headline: White House pushes for Middle East deal as Iran resists concessions
cards.teaser: The Trump administration faces pressure from Gulf allies and domestic polls to end the conflict, but Iran seeks concessions before agreeing to terms.
cards.body:
The White House is working to broker a deal to end the war in the Middle East, facing pressure from both Gulf state allies and domestic political concerns. The administration's diplomatic efforts come as polling appears to be affecting the president's approach to the conflict.

Iran has indicated it wants concessions as part of any agreement. The Iranian position has created an obstacle to the White House's goal of achieving a comprehensive settlement to end the hostilities.

cards.headline: Justice Department to pause work on $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund after court ruling
cards.teaser: The Justice Department said it would abide by a court order pausing its fund for victims of government weaponization, though it strongly disagrees with the ruling.
cards.body:
The Justice Department announced it will comply with a court order halting a $1.776 billion fund created to compensate victims of government "weaponization." Although the department expressed strong disagreement with the court's decision, it said it would follow the ruling.

The fund has faced significant opposition in Congress and the courts throughout its existence. The Trump administration is signaling a retreat from the controversial initiative, which had been a prominent part of its agenda.

cards.headline: Former Colorado clerk Tina Peters released from prison after sentence commuted
cards.teaser: Tina Peters, the former Mesa County clerk convicted in an election security case, has been released from prison.
cards.body:
Former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters was released from prison Monday after President Trump successfully pressured Colorado's Democratic governor to commute her sentence. Peters, a conspiracy theorist convicted in connection with a 2020 election security breach scheme, had served less than a quarter of her nine-year sentence. The 70-year-old's early release was confirmed by the Colorado corrections department.

Peters became a prominent figure among election deniers following her conviction for participating in efforts to promote election conspiracy theories. Her commutation has sparked divided reactions in the Colorado community where she previously served as clerk.

cards.headline: National Republican Senatorial Committee forms joint fundraising committee with Ken Paxton
cards.teaser: The NRSC has joined with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton to establish a joint fundraising operation for his Senate campaign.
cards.body:
The National Republican Senatorial Committee has set up a joint fundraising committee with Ken Paxton following his victory in the Texas Senate GOP primary. The move signals national Republican support for Paxton's general election campaign.

Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear said that Texas is in play for Democrats after Paxton's primary win. The race between Paxton and Democratic candidate James Talarico has turned negative from the start, with analysts describing both candidates as populists.

cards.headline: Police investigate men emerging from New York City sewers
cards.teaser: The NYPD is investigating videos showing people climbing out of manholes in Brooklyn neighborhoods.
cards.body:
Police are investigating videos showing men climbing out of sewers in Brooklyn. The NYPD confirmed that the people emerging from manholes pose no threat to the public.

According to sources, the men are believed to be treasure hunters. Two separate groups were spotted exiting sewers in the Williamsburg and Gravesend neighborhoods.

cards.headline: University student killed while walking home from night out in Southampton
cards.teaser: Henry Nowak was killed in Southampton, and his attacker has been jailed.
cards.body:
A killer described as weapons-obsessed has been jailed for the death of university student Henry Nowak. Nowak was killed as he walked back from a night out in Southampton.

Bodycam footage shown in court captured the victim being handcuffed. The case concluded with the conviction and sentencing of Nowak's killer.

hero.headline: Alphabet to Raise $80 Billion for AI Expansion
hero.body:
Alphabet plans to raise $80 billion through stock sales to fund its artificial intelligence infrastructure, marking one of the largest capital raises in corporate history. The search and technology company will use the proceeds to expand its AI computing capabilities and compete in the rapidly growing AI market.

Berkshire Hathaway will invest $10 billion in Alphabet through a private placement as part of the fundraising effort. The investment by Warren Buffett's company represents a significant vote of confidence in Alphabet's AI strategy and long-term prospects. The remainder of the capital will come from public stock offerings.

The massive fundraising reflects the enormous costs associated with building and maintaining AI systems. Technology companies have been racing to expand their computing infrastructure to train and deploy large language models and other AI tools. The capital will likely fund data centers, specialized chips, and other hardware necessary for AI development.

Alphabet has been working to integrate AI across its product lineup, including search, advertising, cloud computing, and productivity software. The company faces intense competition from Microsoft, which has partnered with OpenAI, and other tech giants investing heavily in AI capabilities. Industry analysts view sufficient capital and computing resources as essential for maintaining competitive positions in the AI market.

The stock sale comes as technology companies worldwide pour hundreds of billions of dollars into AI infrastructure. Alphabet's decision to raise such a substantial amount through equity rather than debt suggests management expects significant returns from AI investments over the coming years. The company has not disclosed a specific timeline for deploying the capital or detailed breakdowns of planned spending across different AI projects.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Climb After U.S.-Iran Military Strikes
cards.teaser: Oil prices rose as the United States and Iran exchanged military fire while continuing diplomatic negotiations.
cards.body:
Oil prices rose 6 percent following military strikes between the United States and Iran over the weekend, including attacks on Iranian sites near Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Investors are assessing the potential impact on global energy supplies amid the escalating tensions.

Analysts cautioned that oil prices could climb substantially higher if the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global oil transport, remains disrupted. Meanwhile, both countries have halted direct negotiations, with Iran suspending talks over U.S. support for Israeli operations in Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: Florida Sues OpenAI Over ChatGPT Safety Claims
cards.teaser: Florida's attorney general filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman alleging safety failures linked to multiple deaths.
cards.body:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company failed to warn users about ChatGPT's potential dangers while marketing it as safe and reliable. The lawsuit claims OpenAI built a "web of deceit" around the chatbot's safety features.

The case centers on violent incidents in Florida, including a shooting at Florida State University, which authorities say involved ChatGPT. The lawsuit represents one of the first major state-level legal challenges targeting an AI company over public safety concerns tied to its products.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Reach Records as Tech Gains Offset Oil Spike
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and other major indexes closed at record highs despite oil prices surging above $97 per barrel.
cards.body:
Major stock indexes reached record levels as technology gains outweighed concerns about rising oil prices. The S&P 500 closed at an all-time high to start trading in the month, while the Dow slipped slightly. Nvidia led the technology sector rally, fueling enthusiasm for AI-related stocks.

Oil prices rose above $97 per barrel due to Middle East tensions, but the increase was not sufficient to derail the broader market rally. Wall Street showed optimism about potential diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran, which helped support investor sentiment. Technology stocks provided the primary boost to overall market performance despite energy sector volatility.

cards.headline: FedEx Freight Begins Trading as Independent Company
cards.teaser: FedEx Freight started trading as a separate publicly listed company after splitting from its parent.
cards.body:
FedEx Freight began trading on the New York Stock Exchange as an independent company following its separation from FedEx. The freight unit's shares fell in their market debut. The spinoff creates a standalone trucking and logistics company separate from the parent corporation's other delivery services.

The company's chief executive said self-driving trucks are ready for widespread commercial use, signaling potential future investments in autonomous vehicle technology. The separation allows FedEx Freight to operate independently and make strategic decisions focused solely on the freight business rather than coordinating with the broader FedEx portfolio.

cards.headline: CBS News Correspondent Criticizes Network Leadership
cards.teaser: Scott Pelley accused CBS News leadership of damaging 60 Minutes during a staff meeting.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, a correspondent for 60 Minutes, criticized CBS News editor in chief Bari Weiss and the show's new executive producer Nick Bilton during a staff meeting. Pelley accused the leadership of harming the long-running Sunday news program.

The confrontation represents a significant internal conflict at one of television's most established news operations. 60 Minutes has been a flagship program for CBS News for decades. The staff meeting turned contentious as Pelley voiced his objections to the current direction under the network's leadership changes.

cards.headline: Energy Department Proposes Limits on Appliance Rebates
cards.teaser: New guidance would prevent consumers from receiving rebates after swapping out appliances under a program funded by the Inflation Reduction Act.
cards.body:
The Energy Department released new guidance that would phase out rebates for consumers who swap old appliances for more efficient models. The proposed rules would prevent people from receiving financial incentives after making such purchases.

The rebate program was established under the Inflation Reduction Act to encourage homeowners to replace older, less efficient appliances with newer models. The proposed changes would alter how the program operates, potentially affecting consumers planning to upgrade their home appliances with government support.

hero.headline: Rams acquire Myles Garrett from Browns in blockbuster trade for Jared Verse
hero.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have acquired star edge rusher Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round draft pick, and additional draft compensation, according to multiple reports from NFL Network and ESPN.

Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since the Browns drafted him first overall in 2017, he has accumulated 125.5 sacks, 413 pressures, and 149 tackles for loss—more than any other player during that span. In 2025, he set an NFL single-season sacks record with 23 catches.

The trade comes after Garrett requested to leave Cleveland last year following the team's disappointing 3-14 season. Seeking a championship opportunity, he subsequently signed a four-year, $160 million extension with the Browns valued at $204.8 million total, making him the highest-paid non-quarterback in league history at the time. Despite his individual excellence, the Browns finished the 2025 season with a 5-12 record and missed the playoffs for the second consecutive year. Garrett was the team's lone All-Pro selection.

The Browns recently fired head coach Kevin Stefanski and replaced him with former Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator Todd Monken. Monken indicated he had not held a face-to-face meeting with Garrett since his hiring.

Verse, the player going to Cleveland, is a 25-year-old edge rusher who was selected in the first round by the Rams in 2024. He earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors and was named to the Pro Bowl this past season despite his youth. The young defender has recorded 12 sacks and 22 tackles for loss in his brief career.

For the Rams, the acquisition addresses defensive needs as they aim to maximize their championship window. The team lost to the Seattle Seahawks in last season's NFC Championship game. The Rams are no strangers to aggressive moves in pursuit of championships, having traded for Matthew Stafford in 2021 with the Detroit Lions. Stafford led the team to a Super Bowl victory in his first season with the franchise.

Super Bowl LXI will be played at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California next February, giving the Rams the opportunity to compete for a title at their home venue.

The trade reshapes the defensive landscape for both franchises. Cleveland faces the challenge of rebuilding its pass rush without its most accomplished defensive player while adding young talent and future draft picks. For Los Angeles, integrating one of the league's premier pass rushers strengthens their playoff contention while signaling a commitment to winning immediately, even at the expense of long-term roster flexibility.

cards.headline: Patriots acquire A.J. Brown from Eagles in blockbuster trade
cards.teaser: The New England Patriots have traded for wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in a major deal.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded three-time Pro Bowl wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots on Monday. In return, the Eagles receive a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027.

The move reunites Brown with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. Brown had grown frustrated during his time in Philadelphia, ending months of speculation about his future with the Eagles.

cards.headline: Giants sign Odell Beckham Jr. in return to New York
cards.teaser: The New York Giants have signed wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr., bringing the veteran back to the team where he began his career.
cards.body:
Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has rejoined the New York Giants, the franchise where he first established himself as a star player 12 years ago. The signing marks his return to competitive football with the team that originally drafted him.

The Giants have also added receivers JuJu Smith-Schuster and Braxton Berrios to strengthen their receiving group, making multiple investments in their passing game this season.

cards.headline: Ben Askren returns to wrestling after double lung transplant
cards.teaser: Former UFC fighter Ben Askren will compete at RAF 11 against Belal Muhammad less than a year after receiving a life-saving double lung transplant.
cards.body:
Askren will face former UFC welterweight champion Muhammad in his first competitive wrestling match since recovering from near-fatal pneumonia that required the transplant procedure. The 39-year-old wrestler has made a remarkable recovery from the health crisis that threatened his life.

The bout at RAF 11 marks a significant milestone in Askren's return to athletic competition. His recovery from the double lung transplant and return to the mat has drawn attention across combat sports. Askren previously competed in both wrestling and mixed martial arts before the health emergency sidelined him.

cards.headline: Illinois lawmakers adjourn without passing Bears stadium funding bill
cards.teaser: The Illinois legislature adjourned without voting on a stadium funding proposal, leaving the Chicago Bears' future location uncertain.
cards.body:
The Illinois House ended its session without taking up a last-minute bill aimed at keeping the Bears in the state, despite the Senate passing stadium legislation. The $55 billion state budget passed without including provisions for a new Bears facility. Governor JB Pritzker indicated he is prepared to accept responsibility if the team relocates.

The Bears have indicated that moving to Indiana remains a possibility following the legislative impasse. The team has been seeking public funding assistance for a new stadium, but state lawmakers could not reach agreement before adjourning. The failure to pass the bill leaves Chicago facing the prospect of losing its NFL franchise to a neighboring state.

cards.headline: Sabalenka advances to French Open quarterfinals with win over Osaka
cards.teaser: World number one Aryna Sabalenka defeated Naomi Osaka in a night session match to reach her fourth consecutive French Open quarterfinal.
cards.body:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka advanced to her fourth consecutive French Open quarterfinal with a hard-fought night session victory over Naomi Osaka. Sabalenka's superior serving proved decisive in overcoming the spirited challenge from her opponent at Roland Garros.

In other quarterfinal action, Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska continued her impressive French Open debut by defeating French player Diane Parry to reach the final eight.

cards.headline: Qualifier Chwalinska reaches French Open quarterfinals
cards.teaser: Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska advanced to the French Open quarterfinals by defeating French player Diane Parry.
cards.body:
Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska defeated French player Diane Parry to advance to the French Open quarterfinals. The victory marks a remarkable achievement in her debut at Roland Garros, having entered the tournament through qualifying rounds.

Chwalinska has now reached the final eight, continuing an unexpected run at the tournament. After her win, the Polish player noted that few people are aware of her, highlighting her status as an emerging talent on the professional tennis circuit.

hero.headline: Marilyn Monroe Fans Gather in Palm Springs for Centennial Birthday Celebration
hero.body:
Fans of Marilyn Monroe traveled to Palm Springs to mark what would have been the actress's 100th birthday. The gathering brought together admirers of the Hollywood icon to celebrate her legacy and cultural impact a century after her birth.

Monroe, born Norma Jeane Mortenson in 1926, became one of the most recognizable figures in American cinema during the 1950s and early 1960s. Her performances in films like "Some Like It Hot" and "Gentlemen Prefer Blondes" cemented her status as a cultural icon. She died in 1962 at age 36.

Beyond her image as a blonde bombshell, Monroe was a shrewd professional who maintained strong friendships and collaborations throughout her career. According to photographer Lawrence Schiller, who worked with Monroe on her final photoshoot in 1962, she possessed remarkable knowledge of photography and light. "Very few people really understand light. Marilyn understood it," Schiller recalled. "She knew a lot about photography, and she knew what was right for her."

Monroe's final nude photoshoot took place on the set of "Something's Got to Give" and was her own publicity stunt, designed to remind studios of her star power. Schiller described how Monroe carefully controlled the creative process, even editing the negatives herself at Schwab's Pharmacy on Sunset Boulevard, cutting up images she disliked.

Monroe also formed meaningful friendships with other women in Hollywood, contrary to her sex-symbol image. Amy Greene, widow of photographer Milton Greene, shared her home with Monroe in the mid-1950s and remembered the skepticism this arrangement provoked. Yet the two became genuine friends. In "Gentlemen Prefer Blondes," Monroe co-starred with Jane Russell, and despite earning only a fraction of Russell's salary, the two developed a lasting affection. Russell later wrote in her 1985 memoir about wishing Monroe could have been present at a beach gathering with close female friends.

The centennial celebration has prompted renewed attention to Monroe's career and influence on popular culture. Multiple media outlets have published retrospectives examining her work as an actress and her careful control over her public image, revealing her to be far more than a superficial celebrity.

Palm Springs served as a retreat for Monroe during her lifetime, making it a fitting location for fans to commemorate the milestone. The city maintains historical connections to Old Hollywood, having attracted celebrities seeking privacy away from Los Angeles during the golden age of cinema.

The centennial has sparked discussions about Monroe's lasting impact on entertainment and American culture. Her image remains instantly recognizable decades after her death, and her story continues to fascinate new generations. The gathering in Palm Springs reflects the enduring appeal of an actress whose career, though cut short, left a permanent mark on Hollywood history.

cards.headline: CBS Names Nick Bilton to Lead 60 Minutes Amid Staff Concerns
cards.teaser: The newsmagazine enters its 59th season under new leadership as it faces staff morale and cost challenges.
cards.body:
CBS News editor in chief Bari Weiss appointed Nick Bilton as executive producer of 60 Minutes, with the program entering its 59th season. The move comes as part of a broader overhaul that included firing the show's previous executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

The shake-up has sparked internal conflict. During a staff meeting with Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle, veteran correspondent Scott Pelley openly criticized Weiss and the decisions, according to sources. The appointment reflects efforts to address longstanding challenges at the newsmagazine, though the changes have deepened tensions among remaining staff members.

cards.headline: RuPaul Stars in Disaster Comedy Stop! That! Train!
cards.teaser: The drag icon teams with Ginger Minj and Jujubee in a film that revisits the disaster comedy genre.
cards.body:
RuPaul joins fellow drag performers Ginger Minj and Jujubee in the new disaster comedy Stop! That! Train! The film blends theatrical performance with the genre, earning praise for its infectious humor and charm. Critics have drawn comparisons to classic disaster comedies like Airplane!

Director Adam Shankman crafted the project to breathe fresh life into the disaster comedy genre through a contemporary lens. The film marks a significant milestone for the RuPaul's Drag Race alumni, who leverage their performance expertise for their theatrical screen debut. RuPaul takes on a character in a position of authority throughout the comedy.

cards.headline: The Lost Boys Stage Musical Receives 12 Tony Nominations
cards.teaser: Tony-winning director Michael Arden adapted the 1987 vampire film for the stage.
cards.body:
Michael Arden directed a stage adaptation of The Lost Boys, the 1987 cult vampire film, which earned 12 Tony nominations this year. Arden won a Tony Award last year for directing a musical about robots.

The Tony-winning director is also developing a Broadway musical adaptation of Happy Feet. His work on The Lost Boys demonstrates his continued focus on bringing unconventional source material to the stage.

cards.headline: Gracie Abrams Announces Third Album Daughter From Hell
cards.teaser: The singer-songwriter will release the album on July 17, calling it her favorite music she has made.
cards.body:
Gracie Abrams announced her third studio album, Daughter From Hell, set for release on July 17. The singer-songwriter described the upcoming record as her favorite music she has ever made.

Abrams has built a following with her confessional songwriting style across her first two albums. The announcement signals a new creative chapter for the artist, who has characterized this collection as representing a high point in her output to date.

cards.headline: Outlander: Blood of My Blood Returns to Starz in September
cards.teaser: The prequel series will premiere its second season on Sept. 18.
cards.body:
Starz set a Sept. 18 premiere date for the second season of Outlander: Blood of My Blood, the prequel to the romantic epic series. The network released the first teaser for the new season.

The first season introduced viewers to the younger versions of central characters Claire and Jamie. The prequel expands the universe of the long-running Outlander franchise, which has maintained a dedicated following across multiple seasons on the premium cable network.

cards.headline: Bad Bunny Performs Surprise Songs and Settles Rivalries on Global Tour
cards.teaser: The Puerto Rican star's recent shows featured unexpected moments and onstage reconciliations.
cards.body:
Bad Bunny included surprise performances of older hits and ended rivalries onstage during his recent global tour dates. The Puerto Rican artist used the tour to create memorable moments beyond his standard setlist.

The tour stops showcased Bad Bunny's willingness to vary his performances and address personal relationships publicly. The approach has generated attention across his international concert dates as fans anticipate which surprise elements might appear at each show.

hero.headline: Trump confronts Netanyahu over Lebanon escalation in expletive-laden call
hero.body:
President Trump engaged in a heated phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over Israel's military escalation in Lebanon, according to two U.S. officials and a third source briefed on the exchange. During the Monday conversation, Trump used profanity to criticize Netanyahu, calling him "crazy" and accusing him of ingratitude. He also intervened to block Israel's planned strike on Beirut.

The confrontation underscores growing tensions between the Trump administration and Netanyahu's government as the region faces mounting instability. The call came after Iran warned it would withdraw from ongoing negotiations with the United States in response to Israeli military operations in Lebanon. That same day, Netanyahu announced he had ordered the military to escalate its offensive against Hezbollah, stating his goal was to "crush" the organization.

According to the sources, Trump told Netanyahu that attacking Beirut would further damage Israel's international standing. One U.S. official noted that Trump referenced his past support for Netanyahu, suggesting the prime minister should be grateful for American backing. The decision to halt the planned strike represented an unusual constraint on Israeli military operations that reflected the seriousness of the dispute.

The escalating conflict in Lebanon has intensified despite a ceasefire that began in April. Both Israel and Hezbollah have continued exchanging fire on a near-daily basis. In recent days, Israel has carried out extensive airstrikes across southern Lebanon, the Bekaa Valley, and areas near Tyre. Lebanese authorities report that Israeli strikes since March have killed more than 3,100 people. Hezbollah has responded with drone attacks on Israeli military positions and border areas, with multiple strikes occurring on Monday.

Netanyahu's call for intensified operations has found support among far-right members of his government. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for ending the threat posed by Hezbollah's drone attacks, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir demanded a return to intensive warfare and expansion of Israeli-controlled territory.

The situation reflects broader complications in Middle East diplomacy. Iran's decision to threaten withdrawal from U.S. negotiations signals how Israeli military actions directly influence diplomatic engagement with Tehran. However, Trump expressed indifference about the status of those talks during a separate Monday interview with CNBC, stating he did not care whether negotiations with Iran continued, calling them "very boring."

The disconnect between Trump's intervention to block the Beirut strike and his dismissive comments about Iran talks creates uncertainty about the administration's strategic priorities. The U.S.-Israel relationship and prospects for broader regional diplomacy remain in flux as the conflict continues to develop and both sides pursue escalation.

cards.headline: Trump administration requires most Medicaid beneficiaries to work
cards.teaser: A new rule mandates that most Medicaid recipients between 19 and 64 prove employment, community service, or work program participation to receive benefits.
cards.body:
The Trump administration issued a final rule requiring most Medicaid beneficiaries between the ages of 19 and 64 to demonstrate they work, complete community service, or participate in a work program to qualify for benefits. The rule establishes standards that states must follow when implementing the Medicaid work requirements mandated by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

The rule outlines broad policies each state is required to have in place when enforcing the new work requirements. The change represents a significant shift in how the federal health insurance program for low-income Americans operates, adding employment conditions to eligibility criteria that previously focused primarily on income levels.

cards.headline: Pentagon bars reporters from press office, designates area classified
cards.teaser: The Defense Department has closed its press office to journalists and designated the space as classified, ending years of direct reporter access.
cards.body:
The Pentagon barred reporters from entering the building's press office and designated the facility as a classified space, ending access journalists have had for years. The Defense Department's public affairs office previously allowed reporters to approach military public affairs officials without escorts and ask questions directly.

The change curtails a longstanding arrangement that gave journalists working space within the Pentagon and direct access to public affairs staff. Reporters will no longer be able to enter the area where they could interact with military communications officials on an informal basis.

cards.headline: Rights groups sue over conditions at largest U.S. immigration detention center
cards.teaser: The ACLU and other organizations filed a lawsuit accusing ICE of abuse and inhumane conditions at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas.
cards.body:
Human rights groups including the American Civil Liberties Union filed a lawsuit accusing Immigration and Customs Enforcement of abuse and inhumane conditions at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas, the largest immigration detention center in the U.S. The ACLU, Human Rights Watch, the Texas Civil Rights Project and other organizations brought the case.

The lawsuit targets conditions at the facility, which serves as the primary detention center for ICE in terms of capacity. The legal action seeks to address what the groups characterize as systemic problems with how detainees are treated at the Texas facility.

cards.headline: Sexting scandal threatens Democratic Senate candidate in Maine
cards.teaser: Democrat Graham Platner's Senate campaign faces turmoil after reports he sent sexually explicit messages to multiple women other than his wife.
cards.body:
A sexting scandal threatens the Senate campaign of Democrat Graham Platner, who had been seen as the party's strongest challenger to longtime Republican incumbent Sen. Susan Collins in Maine. Platner reportedly sent sexually explicit messages to multiple women, which his wife, Amy Gertner, discovered in spring 2025. Gertner notified Platner's campaign last year.

The revelations could derail what had been considered an insurgent campaign with potential to unseat Collins. Maine Gov. Janet Mills, who suspended her own Democratic primary campaign but remains on the ballot, reminded voters that she has not withdrawn from the race as the party weighs the fallout from the Platner story.

cards.headline: Trump ends rebate program for switching to electric appliances
cards.teaser: The Energy Department reinterpreted an Inflation Reduction Act program, eliminating cash rebates for Americans who purchase high-efficiency electric appliances.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has eliminated a rebate program that provided cash incentives for homeowners to purchase high-efficiency electric appliances. The Energy Department issued new guidance reinterpreting the initiative, which was created through the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act to encourage Americans to transition from gas to electric appliances.

The rebate mechanism, established by Congress two years prior, is no longer available under the Trump administration's revised interpretation of the program.

cards.headline: Trump ally convicted in Colorado election case released early from prison
cards.teaser: A Colorado county clerk convicted of interference in the 2020 elections was released from jail early after President Trump pressured the state's governor.
cards.body:
Tina Peters, a former Colorado county clerk and conspiracy theorist, was released from prison Monday after President Trump pressured the state's Democratic governor to commute her sentence. Peters had been convicted of participating in a scheme to advance election conspiracy theories promoted by Trump following the 2020 election.

The 70-year-old served less than a quarter of her original nine-year sentence before her early release. The Colorado corrections department confirmed her release but declined to provide further details about Peters.
